summary: Selected papers emphasize ab initio nuclear-structure inputs for O-O and Ne-Ne flow interpretation, femtoscopic biases in hyperon spin correlations, pre-equilibrium photon production, quarkonium spectral functions, small-x/eikonal theory, HEP reconstruction ML, neural kinetic equations, and cautionary validation failures in PINNs, neural surrogates, and CNN-based spectroscopy claims.
strongest_paper: 2608.22699: ab initio decomposition of quadrupole correlations in O-16 and Ne-20 directly supports interpretation of LHC light-ion flow measurements.

papers.title: Ab initio anatomy of quadrupole correlations in O-16 and Ne-20
papers.authors: Chenrong Ding, Benjamin Bally, Stavros Bofos, Thomas Duguet, Yi Li, Jiangming Yao
papers.abstract: Ab initio nuclear-structure analysis isolates antisymmetrization, collective rotational and vibrational, and non-collective dynamical contributions to mean-square quadrupole eccentricity, explaining why classical-rotor interpretations of O-O and Ne-Ne flow can work despite many-body correlations.

papers.title: Eikonal Expansion for Classical Gluon Fields: from Weak to Strong
papers.authors: Shane Brown, Alex DeBrizzi, Alex Kovner
papers.abstract: Formal eikonal expansion for classical gluon fields shows that weak-field counting is straightforward but strong-field nonlinearities mix eikonal orders; integrating out high-longitudinal-momentum modes yields renormalized low-momentum currents.

papers.title: Effects of femtoscopic correlations on spin-spin correlation measurements
papers.authors: Bijun Fan, Like Liu, Shusu Shi
papers.abstract: AMPT plus spin-dependent Lednicky-Lyuboshits weights shows that femtoscopic effects can induce apparent Lambda-Lambda and Lambda-antiLambda spin correlations, especially at low q_inv, at magnitudes comparable to preliminary CMS-scale measurements.

papers.title: Photon production from gluon splitting and fusion induced by a magnetic field of arbitrary strength in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.authors: Alejandro Ayala, Santiago Bernal-Langarica, Jose Jorge Medina-Serna, Ana Julia Mizher
papers.abstract: Pre-equilibrium photon yield and v2 are computed from magnetic-field-induced gluon splitting and fusion with glasma-inspired and anisotropic gluon distributions, with reported agreement with PHENIX direct-photon data.

papers.title: Charmonia at Finite Momentum and Spatial Correlators in Quark-Gluon Plasma
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic T-matrix calculations with finite momentum, screened potentials, heavy-quark selfenergies, and particle-hole zero modes qualitatively reproduce lattice-QCD Euclidean and spatial charmonium correlator trends.

papers.title: Down-Type Jet Identification in Fully Hadronic ttbar Events
papers.abstract: A two-stage GNN+Transformer and hybrid assignment/classifier with a conditional diffusion head reconstructs down-type jets in all-hadronic ttbar events and preserves useful spin-correlation information.

papers.title: Neural Boltzmann Equations
papers.abstract: Neural particle distribution functions, Monte Carlo phase-space integration with collider-style importance sampling, and natural-gradient evolution are combined to solve high-dimensional Boltzmann equations and compute N_eff in the early universe.

papers.title: Inverted model selection in physics-informed neural networks: when a lower residual selects a worse solution
papers.abstract: Matched PINN variants can obtain lower equation residuals while violating structural identities by orders of magnitude; a lexicographic admissibility gate is proposed before residual comparison.

papers.title: When a neural surrogate cannot accelerate a solver: runtime share, closed-loop drift, and the economics of uncertainty gating in a stiff coupled simulation
papers.abstract: A controlled negative result for a neutrino-radiation/matter solver surrogate shows that runtime share, closed-loop distribution shift, fallback cost, and directed bias can erase per-call ML speedups.

papers.title: Revisiting the Lambda(1405) pole structure with convolutional neural networks
papers.authors: Julius B. Pagayon, Vince Angelo A. Chavez, Denny Lane B. Sombillo
papers.abstract: CNN classification of near-degenerate Lambda(1405) lineshape variations is used to infer dominant pole structures; the transfer from classifier consensus to analytic pole claims appears potentially overstrong without visible amplitude-model and systematic controls.
